name: write_logic_many
summary: Write up to 256 logic values in order in one call; each result stands alone, by index, with its own error.

help.text: Each result is {index, ok, reference_id, logic_type, requested_value, previous_value, current_value} (current_value read back and driven_by present as in write_logic), or {index, ok: false, reference_id, logic_type, error}; reference_id and logic_type are null when the entry's own could not be read. Each write runs the write lint rules as write_logic does (see lint): a refusal (lint_refused) fails only its entry and the others still run, and allow_lint covers every entry. Warnings are listed once for the call, each with its entry's index. A report (dry_run) checks each write against the world as it stands, without the writes before it, and writes nothing: results of {index, ok, reference_id, logic_type, requested_value, previous_value, opens} (driven_by present as in write_logic), each refused entry also a problem with its index (see report_only).
help.keys: report_only, problems, gateway_id, results, count, success_count, error_count, warnings.

logic_type.description: A logic type name (Temperature) or number.

value.description: The value to write: a finite number.

writes.description: The writes, up to 256, each {reference_id, logic_type, value}, applied in order.

allow_lint.description: Default false: an entry that opens a device onto a network a write lint rule finds a problem on fails (lint_refused); true writes it anyway.

dry_run.description: Default false. true checks every write, the write lint rules included, and writes nothing; the reply starts report_only (see report_only).
